projects.name: Copart Dealer Digital
projects.summary: Lead tracker site for dealer sales, built from pre-start work: AEO baseline, DFW dealer map and scoring, and state dealer license leads. Leads now cover 28 states plus DC (92,492 leads), focused on car and wholesale dealers. Live on Vercel. Public data only.
built: AEO baseline (Sep 27): 25 dealer questions through the ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini APIs. Results in aeo/runs/2026-09-27/summary.md
AEO headline: Copart named in 50% of answers to the 20 unbranded questions (30 of 60). All questions: Copart 60%, Manheim 61%, ACV 52%
AEO by engine: Claude 68%, ChatGPT 60%, Gemini 52%. By stage: Awareness 56%, Compare 94%, Membership 67%, Selling 33% (weakest on every engine)

AEO biggest gaps: "Best dealer-only auctions in Texas" and "Online auction vs wholesaler for trade-ins" (Copart missing on all 3 engines), plus other trade-in selling questions. Most cited sites: copart.com, acvauctions.com, iaai.com
AEO runner now uses a higher length limit by default (8 Claude answers were cut off and re-run)
AEO side test (not in baseline): Claude Code agents with web search named Copart 88% of the time, but position it as the place for damaged and salvage cars, not general wholesale
DFW dealer dataset: 36 independent dealers in data/dealers.json, every field sourced, all still verified: false; 2,414 units in the Sep 27 inventory snapshot

Two scores: seller fit (older, high-mileage stock, sell-your-car page, buy here pay here) and buyer fit (newer license, smaller lot, lower prices). 14 dealers unscored because their inventory pages are drawn by script

Map app (/map), deployed and live: password protected and refuses access if no password is set; works on a phone; seller/buyer toggle; each dealer shows score reasons, sources, brief and pitch draft; Resources section with prompts, demo script and AEO summary
Top 20 lead list in leads/dfw-top-20.csv and .md. Top 3: CityWide Motors, Lone Star Motors II, L&C Auto Sales
Three draft pre-call briefs in briefs/: Gulliver (large), Lone Star Motors II (mid), CityWide (small). Each sourced, ends with suggested fixes to the brief prompt
Supporting docs: Monday demo script, 30/60/90 plan, research brief, week one questions for Ken and IT, deploy doc
TxDMV statewide list: 20,935 licenses at 16,272 locations; 2,999 in the Dallas, Tarrant and Collin territory (Collin added so Plano lots match); 1,080 first licensed in the last 12 months

Lead books: 15,287 leads in A/B/C tiers (1,614 A, 3,796 B, 9,877 C) across 12 regions. DFW has 3,803 leads, 373 tier A. One category per lead sets base points. Scoring explained in docs/lead-playbook.md
Key accounts: 303 dealer groups covering 2,041 rooftops

Leads section: overview, call list per region with filters and CSV, key accounts, new licenses (last 30 days: 173, 116 new dealers, 57 adding a license), wholesalers (555 locations), weekly changes page, statewide map with distance to nearest Copart and competitor auction. Copart blue (PMS 300), mobile friendly

Weekly change tracking: data/license_changes.py compares each TxDMV snapshot to the last. First comparison (Sep 27 to 29): 1 new license, 1 dropped. Excludes Copart locations, other auctions, retail chains and expired licenses
Excel books per region plus master with tracker columns
Opening lines and call guidance removed from the site and books at Chase's request. The data stays
Contact info is not in git: phone and email files live in leads/txdmv/ (gitignored). Only counts are committed

All 50 states plus DC checked and logged (Oct 1). 28 states plus DC built with 92,492 dealer leads. Added Oct 1: Arkansas, Colorado, Delaware, Mississippi (franchise stores only), Nebraska, Nevada, North Dakota, Rhode Island, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, Virginia, DC. Colorado, Rhode Island, Tennessee and Utah came from hand-downloaded files; the rest the pipeline pulls on its own
22 states have no usable public list: 9 no public list, 6 one-dealer-at-a-time lookup only, 5 state sells the list, 2 newest list too old
All states page under Leads: US tile map plus a row per state with source, date, lead count, and for states without leads, what was checked and the by-hand next step

Indiana merged with Leo's lists: added 113 credit unions (all 8 of ours were on his) and 421 tow, rental, salvage and dealer companies (69 strong matches, 35 weak left off, 4 competitor auctions and officer names left off). Indiana went from 3,865 to 4,396 leads. Both comparison CSVs are with Chase

Lead tables rebuilt around facts: the state's own license types (lines of business) replaced "play"; scores and tiers hidden on every Leads page (still calculated for checking against Copart Dealer Sales results later); quick filters All, Car dealers, Wholesale, Specialty, plus Has phone and Has email; every column sorts, plus a Sort menu (distance, miles to Copart, newest license, first licensed, units sold, group size); region lists include wholesale-only dealers
Fixed: two leads sharing a license number made rows jump or open in pairs
Look and feel: lead maps on a light gray background, dots colored by type (wholesale gold, car dealers blue, other gray); dark mode across the site with an Auto, Light and Dark picker
Records: docs/decisions.md and the change log in docs/handoff-leads.md cover every change. Oct 1: 14 commits, 7 production deploys

notes.title: Potential Agents to Add:
body: Pre-visit briefing agent. Each morning, it builds a short card for each stop on today's leg: past notes, who to ask for, which pitch to lead with, and what's on the dealer's lot from their own website. It saves reps from scrolling notes in the parking lot.

Weekly digest agent. It reads the sync log and emails Ken or the team lead a summary of stops visited per rep, hot leads, dealers that went quiet, and anything flagged for a return visit. It's cheap to build because the data already exists.
CDS handoff agent. When a visit is marked as interested, it drafts the handoff to the CDS rep with everything gathered so far. It can also draft a follow-up text for the field rep to send.
For scaling to new yards

Route builder agent. You give it a yard address and it researches about 30 dealers, checks each address and phone against real sources, groups them into legs, and outputs the dealer list with confidence flags and caveats. This replaces the most manual part of the project. It has to follow the "never invent dealer data" rule: every entry cites its source, and a person approves the list before it ships.

Freshness checker. Once a month, it re-verifies every dealer on active routes for closures, phone changes, or new owners, then flags changes for review instead of overwriting them. The sourcing doc already says lists go stale.

Road-added dealer enrichment. When a rep adds a dealer they spotted on the road, with just a name and a GPS pin, the agent looks up the address, phone, and website. It fills the gaps marked "Verify first" and never presents its guesses as confirmed.
